subjective: Oreo has had blood and mucus in his stool one to two times over the past one to two days. He has not been on any medication for this issue. There are no other known medical conditions. Oreo's appetite is poor; he has not eaten anything today and ate only a little yesterday. Water intake is normal. Blood in stool was first noticed two days ago in the afternoon, with small amounts continuing since this morning. The owner reports Oreo only eats when administered by a medical person and refuses food otherwise.
objective: Veterinarian plans to check Oreo's temperature and perform a general physical examination. Weight is approximately 8 kilograms as reported by the owner, to be confirmed. No other physical examination findings or vital signs were documented during this consultation.
assessment: Suspected inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) causing blood and mucus in stool and loose motions. The condition is considered not curable but manageable with dietary modifications and supportive care. Poor appetite noted, likely related to gastrointestinal upset. No other medical conditions reported.
plan: Diagnostic: Recommend blood test after three days to assess underlying condition. Therapeutic: Administer probiotic sachet (entero probiotic) mixed with curd or water twice daily. Provide chicken broth with a little rice and curd as a bland diet. Prescribe a tonic powder to help manage dysentery symptoms; mix with food for administration. Avoid antibiotics at this stage. Monitoring: Observe Oreo's stool and general condition for the next two days. If no improvement, reassess and consider further diagnostics or treatment. Owner Instructions: Mix medicines with curd or water for easier administration. Take Oreo's temperature and monitor water intake and appetite. Continue bland diet and probiotics. Follow-up: Re-evaluate after two days or sooner if condition worsens.
conclusion: Oreo, an approximately 8 kg Airedale Terrier, presents with blood and mucus in stool over the past one to two days, accompanied by poor appetite but normal water intake. The veterinarian suspects inflammatory bowel disease, which is not curable but manageable with dietary modifications including chicken broth, curd, and rice, along with probiotic and tonic powder administration. A blood test is recommended after three days. The owner is advised to monitor Oreo's temperature, stool, and general condition, and to administer medications mixed with food or water. Follow-up is planned in two days to assess response to treatment.
key_issues:
1. Blood and mucus in stool with loose motions, suspected inflammatory bowel disease. Remarks: Condition is managed with diet and supportive care; requires monitoring and possible further diagnostics.
2. Poor appetite and difficulty administering medication. Remarks: Owner advised to mix medicines with curd or water to facilitate administration.
abnormal_findings: Presence of blood and mucus in stool as reported by owner. Poor appetite noted. No other abnormal findings documented.
customer_instructions: Administer probiotic sachet mixed with curd or water twice daily. Provide bland diet consisting of chicken broth, curd, and rice. Mix tonic powder with food for administration. Take Oreo's temperature regularly. Monitor water intake, appetite, and stool consistency. Observe for any worsening of symptoms. Follow up after two days or sooner if condition deteriorates.
reminders: Owner to monitor Oreo's temperature, stool, appetite, and water intake daily. Blood test to be done after three days. Follow-up consultation scheduled or advised after two days to reassess condition and response to treatment.
